## Preprocessing

We extracted text from each page's headers and paragraphs, then removed URLs, emails, punctuation and numbers, and converted everything to lowercase. Unlike the starter pipeline, we kept every page: the starter code dropped pages without a standard HTML declaration (25 training pages and 14 test pages). Pages with no usable text, such as PDFs and download errors, are predicted as "N/A: No relevant content" (32 test pages). Labeled data was split 80/20 into training and validation sets, stratified by multiclass label, and all models were evaluated on the same validation set.

## Models

**Binary model.** A neural network with a TF-IDF input layer over single words and word pairs (20,000-term vocabulary), one hidden layer of 64 units, and 50% dropout.

**Multiclass model.** A neural network with a TF-IDF input layer over single words (10,000-term vocabulary), one hidden layer of 64 units, and 40% dropout. Adding word pairs did not improve multiclass accuracy, so the simpler model was kept.

**Comparison.** As a baseline, we fit elastic-net logistic regression on principal components of the word TF-IDF matrix.

## Results

| Model                                 | Binary accuracy | Multiclass accuracy |
|---------------------------------------|-----------------|---------------------|
| **Neural network (final)**            | **0.825**       | **0.829**           |
| Elastic-net logistic PCR (baseline)\* | 0.790           | 0.733               |

\*Baseline figures were computed on an earlier validation split and exclude pages with no usable text, so the comparison is approximate.

Both neural networks outperformed the baseline and were used for the final test-set predictions.

## Limitations

The multiclass model under-predicts the smallest category, "Other claim content" (2.4% of test predictions vs. 4.7% of training pages). Validation accuracy was also used to choose models and stop training, so it may slightly overstate accuracy on new pages.
